subject: Next steps: SDK quickstart & local test plan for Novus Health integration
body:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Liu <katie@novushealth.com>, Marco Rivera <marco@novushealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: SDK quickstart & local test plan for Novus Health integration

Hi Katie / Marco —

Thanks again for the call today. Wanted to capture the agreed next steps for the technical pilot and give the team a runnable quickstart you can use locally. TL;DR: we think a Python backend + TS frontend sample will get you to a demo in ~48 hours.

Quick summary of what we heard today:
- Use case: conversational triage + contextual search over clinical KB and internal SOPs (500k docs, ~500MB embeddings)
- Priority features: low-latency generation for triage, embeddings + reranker for search accuracy, structured tool-calling for appointment actions
- Non-functional: data residency in us-west, strict PII retention policy, procurement will want SOC2 and data flow diagram

Action items (owners & rough ETA):
1) Diego: deliver SDK quickstart bundle (Python + TS) and local-run checklist — by 2026-10-06 EOD. (attached zip)
2) Lauren: confirm auth pattern and provide example for server-side token exchange (2026-10-06)
3) Rishi: sample reranker pipeline (FAISS index + candidate scoring) and local test prompts (2026-10-07 AM)
4) Katie / Marco: share procurement contact and any additional compliance docs they need (ASAP)

Quickstart notes (runnable):
- Pre-reqs: Python 3.10+, Node 18+, Docker (for local proxy), pip/npm installed
- Layout in sdk-quickstart-samples.zip: /python-backend, /ts-frontend, /docs/ (runbook + env matrix)

Python quickstart (server-side generation + embeddings):
1) unzip sdk-quickstart-samples.zip && cd python-backend
2) python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
3) pip install -r requirements.txt
4) export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<dev-token>"
   export REDWOOD_ENV=staging
   export REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2
5) python app.py --mode=local

Notes: the quickstart uses the local proxy (docker-compose) to emulate our hosted routing decisions (hosted vs dedicated). The app will log which route was chosen.

TypeScript frontend quickstart (client + tool calling shim):
1) cd ts-frontend && npm ci
2) cp .env.example .env && edit REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8080
3) npm start

The frontend uses a small wrapper to call a server-side /generate endpoint (server holds API key). For security we discourage storing REDWOOD_API_KEY in the browser.

Auth & routing notes:
- For pilot we recommend Server-to-Server Client Credentials (short-lived tokens) for backend tasks (embeddings + rerank)
- Browser flows (user sign-in + tool-calls) can use an OIDC redirect on your auth provider and a server-side token exchange endpoint
- CORS: the quickstart server includes CORS preflight handling for localhost:3000 and your staging domain
- Routing: sample config shows policy 'latency-first' for triage generation and 'cost-first' for background batch embeddings. You can override by setting ROUTING_POLICY=dedicated:high-throughput in .env

Structured output & tool calling:
- We include a json-schema for the appointment tool. Example structured response expected from model (JSON):
  {
    "tool": "create_appointment",
    "args": {
      "patient_id": "string",
      "timeslot": "ISO8601 string"
    }
  }
- The TS shim demonstrates on-the-fly validation of the model's structured output; invalid payloads are rejected and the model is re-prompted (see docs/retries.md)

Embeddings & reranker guidance:
- Use 1536-d embeddings for initial pilot (balanced accuracy); if you need smaller index size we can pilot 768-d quantized vectors
- Reranker pipeline in samples: candidate retrieval (FAISS IVFPQ) -> top-25 -> neural rerank (small cross-encoder) -> final score threshold 0.45 (tunable)
- For local testing Rishi included a small dataset (10k rows) and test harness (scripts/run_rerank_test.sh)

Attachments: postcall-notes.pdf (meeting notes), sdk-quickstart-samples.zip (code + docker-compose), novus-mutation-policy.docx (data handling draft)

Please try the quickstart and call out any blockers. If you want, we can set up a 1-hr working session to pair on local setup — I have availability Wed 10/07 10-12 PT and Thu 10/08 9-11 PT.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Katie Liu <katie@novushealth.com>

Cc: Marco Rivera <marco@novushealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: SDK quickstart & local test plan for Novus Health integration

Diego —

Appreciate the recap and the zip. A couple quick clarifications from our engineering team:
1) Embedding size — you suggest 1536-d. Can you share expected RAM/GB for 500k docs? We need to check infra costs.
2) Auth — we need confirmation we can integrate with our OIDC provider and not expose any tokens client-side. We prefer server-side token exchange.
3) Reranker — if the neural reranker is a small cross-encoder, can we run it on CPU during the pilot?

Also procurement asked for a simple diagram of data flow (even a PPT) showing what leaves our VPC. Can you attach that?

Thanks,
Katie
Katie Liu
Head of Product, Novus Health

On Wed, Oct 6, 2026 at 09:28 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
> To: Katie Liu <katie@novushealth.com>, Marco Rivera <marco@novushealth.com>

> Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2026 09:28:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: Next steps: SDK quickstart & local test plan for Novus Health integration
>
> Katie —
>
> Great questions, here are concise answers and a short code example for server-side token exchange.
>
> 1) Embedding RAM estimate (rough):
> - 1536-d float32 (no quant) -> 1536 * 4 bytes = 6144 bytes per vector (~6KB)
> - 500k vectors -> ~3.0 GB in RAM (plus index overhead ~1.5GB) -> plan for ~4.5–5 GB total for the index in pilot
> - 768-d quantized vectors (int8/4-bit) can reduce on-disk size and RAM by ~2–3x
>
> 2) Auth pattern:
> - Server-side: recommended (Client Credentials + short-lived tokens). We provide example endpoint: /auth/exchange that accepts your OIDC id_token and returns a scoped redwood_session token for backend calls.
> - Browser: use OIDC redirect -> send id_token to server -> server validates + exchanges -> server stores short-lived redwood_session in an HttpOnly cookie
>
> Example Node snippet (exchange endpoint):
> const express = require('express');
> app.post('/auth/exchange', async (req, res) => {
>   const { id_token } = req.body;
>   // validate id_token with your IdP then call Redwood token exchange
>   const resp = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/token/exchange', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }, body: JSON.stringify({ id_token }) });
>   const data = await resp.json();
>   res.cookie('redwood_session', data.token, { httpOnly: true, secure: true });
>   res.sendStatus(200);
> });
>
> 3) Reranker on CPU: small cross-encoders can run on CPU for low QPS (pilot). If you need sub-200ms latencies under concurrency, we'll recommend a small GPU or a faster quantized path. For pilot scale (10–20 QPS) CPU is acceptable.
>
> 4) Data flow diagram: attaching a one-slide diagram (postcall-notes.pdf). If procurement needs a full PPT we can expand.
>
> Happy to run a security walkthrough with your infra team — loop in whoever owns VPC/network.
>
> Cheers,
>Lauren Bishop
>Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
>

Subject: Re: Next steps: SDK quickstart & local test plan for Novus Health integration

Katie / Diego —

Adding a few practical tips for local testing and reranker resource planning:
- Local reranker: the samples include a CPU-friendly PyTorch cross-encoder saved with quantized weights (dynamic quant). To run: pip install -r requirements-rerank.txt && python run_rerank.py --index ./data/test.index
- FAISS index builder: scripts/build_faiss.sh (dockerized) — for 500k you can build on a 16GB RAM dev box if you use on-disk ivf+pq and batch insertion
- Example test commands:
  - python tests/generate_smoke.py --prompt "Find the best triage doc for 'chest pain'"
  - node tests/ts-smoke.js --host http://localhost:8080 --sample 10
- Logging & assertions: test harness asserts the structured tool JSON follows the schema and will flag malformed outputs (useful to iterate prompts)

If you want I can join the working session to pair on index build.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
